answer.answer: Revised child checkpoint committed as checkpoint:701e96f4-6fe2-0807-3668-2285703f0b22. The buildable plan uses three occupied level-0 cores—one required heavy machine per core—and forbids relying on disputed amplifiers or non-Update-1 equipment.

claims.value: The recovered architecture is a modular, distributed backbone-and-spurs network: rails carry items and power, production remains split across sites, rail trunks are upgraded only when measured aggregation requires it, and future, hidden, or unverified equipment is excluded.

Revision N+1 requires one 500-heat Constructorizer plus two 650-heat Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0. Their heavy-machine load is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 heat; each level-0 core provides 1,000 capacity, and exceeding that threshold disables Fire Wave protection.

The safe revised layout uses three occupied level-0 cores: Core A has the Constructorizer alone at 500 heat with 500 nominal capacity remaining; Cores B and C each have one Facturer alone at 650 heat with 350 nominal capacity remaining. Constructorizer+Facturer (1,150), Facturer+Facturer (1,300), and all three together (1,800) are unsafe co-locations and are rejected; all additional local heat must fit inside the stated remainder.

Before building, inspect three candidate Core panels and prepare complete local heat ledgers: existing/support heat + 500 must be at most 1,000 for Core A, and existing/support heat + 650 must be at most 1,000 for each Facturer core. Use only confirmed Update 1 unlocks, do not count disputed amplifier capacity or future/hidden equipment, recheck Fire Wave protection after placement, and validate all three sites through the next Fire Wave before scaling.

No two required heavy machines may share a level-0 core.
decisions: Preserve the distributed backbone-and-spurs architecture and connect sites using confirmed Update 1 rail tiers and unlocked components.
Reject Constructorizer+Facturer, Facturer+Facturer, and three-machine co-location because each exceeds 1,000 heat.
Count existing load and every support building against its local core before construction.
Do not rely on disputed amplifier figures, hidden buildings, future equipment, Rail v.4/v.5, or endgame assumptions.

Prepare full per-core heat ledgers and proceed only if each complete total is at most 1,000 without amplifier assumptions.
Place one required heavy machine per passing core, then recheck Fire Wave protection.

answer.answer: Advanced Straylight from evaluation into implementation and committed child checkpoint checkpoint:58869d64-ac83-c260-49f3-667527ebe5c9 at corpus generation 3606.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first portable context and durable-work layer, not primarily a notes or retrieval product; it preserves durable knowledge together with evidence, decisions, artifacts, checkpoints, and the live state needed to resume and advance work.

The earlier token result is a regression context-volume result, not an uncached-input cost comparison for the persistent API: one-shot BM25 achieved 17/20 cases and 48/53 evidence items at about 1,070 mean estimated tokens, while workspace policy 0.2 achieved 17/20 and 46/53 at about 2,932. The new gate requires persistent-session reporting to separate cumulative cached replay from newly supplied uncached input; BM25 remains a regression fixture, not the target architecture.

The first persistent build slice is a durable workspace pinned to revision N that refreshes to N+1 with a source-bearing diff, provides typed batched query/read using exact and lexical retrieval behind a pluggable semantic interface, and atomically commits an immutable child checkpoint naming its parent and preserving source references.

The transition gate passes only when every case matches direct-filesystem answer claims, completes in no more than four workspace calls, exposes the N-to-N+1 changed constraint, avoids full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice, commits a child with exact parent/revision/source lineage, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input; BM25 17/20, 48/53, and about 1,070 mean estimated tokens remains the regression baseline.

checkpoint.objective: Build and validate the first persistent, snapshot-pinned Straylight workspace transition slice so a fresh agent can resume revision N, incorporate the N+1 delta, advance work, and persist an evidence-linked child without reconstructing the corpus.
current_state: The product thesis remains an agent-first portable context and durable-work layer that preserves durable knowledge plus live resumable work state.
Explicit project-owner authority has moved the project from evaluation into implementation; the BM25 shell is now a regression fixture and the persistent snapshot-pinned workspace is the target.
The prior token figures are regression context-volume measurements; persistent API evaluation must distinguish cumulative cached replay from uncached input.

decisions: Implement resume, revision refresh with source-bearing diff, typed batched retrieval, and immutable child commit as one vertical slice.
Start with exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic-provider boundary and deterministic degraded behavior.
Defer canonical storage-engine selection, broad object modeling, and dreaming mutation beyond this slice.
Never present the prior 2,932-versus-1,070 estimates as persistent API uncached-input costs.
open_questions: Which semantic provider should back the pluggable path after exact and lexical behavior passes the transition harness?
Which persistent store should become canonical after the slice proves its transition invariants?
next_actions: Define typed contracts and persistence schema for workspaces, pinned revisions, parent checkpoints, deltas, batched query/read, source references, and child checkpoints.
Implement exact and lexical retrieval with the semantic-provider interface.

Build the N-to-N+1 transition harness and enforce the four-call ceiling, direct-filesystem claim parity, lineage validation, no unnecessary corpus reconstruction, and separate cached/uncached token reporting.
